recent_posts.Post Message: In this Spotlight edition of the Sabin Vaccine Wire, we reflect on Sabin’s 2025 outbreak response and the evolving global immunization landscape.     When Ethiopia faced its first-ever Marburg outbreak, the country requested swift assistance — and we were able to leverage prior experience and existing partnerships to deliver our vaccine candidate as quickly as possible. We also spent the year thoughtfully recalibrating our global immunization strategy, staying focused on evidence, equity, and country leadership amid public health disruption.     Read reflections from CEO Amy Finan, President of R&D Kelly Lyn Warfield, and President of Global Immunization Rebecca Martin.

This Valentine's Day, help us ditch toxic relationships with disease around the world. 🌍💔  Make a donation to Sabin and support our mission to ensure all people, everywhere receive the benefits of vaccines.   🔗: https://secure.givelively.org/donate/the-albert-b-sabin-vaccine-institute-inc

🌍 "We know health threats don't stop at borders."  Join Sabin President of Global Immunization Rebecca Martin at WHX Dubai on February 10 to explore global health security solutions.  🕥 Keynote "Immunization at the Frontline of Global Health Security: Levers, Lessons, and Leadership" begins at 10:40 AM in the Connect Conference Center.   See you there!

As we work to #TakeOnTyphoid, we face challenges like antimicrobial resistance, lack of #WASH infrastructure, and health care systems in need of improvement.   In this conversation with Dr. Matthew Laurens (@laurens_matt), Director of the Typhoid Vaccine Acceleration Consortium https://x.com/sabinvaccine/status/2023802169284067455/photo/1

top_post.post_message: In this Spotlight edition of the Sabin Vaccine Wire, we reflect on Sabin’s 2025 outbreak response and the evolving global immunization landscape.     When Ethiopia faced its first-ever Marburg outbreak, the country requested swift assistance — and we were able to leverage prior experience and existing partnerships to deliver our vaccine candidate as quickly as possible. We also spent the year thoughtfully recalibrating our global immunization strategy, staying focused on evidence, equity, and country leadership amid public health disruption.     Read reflections from CEO Amy Finan, President of R&D Kelly Lyn Warfield, and President of Global Immunization Rebecca Martin.

✈️ Developing vaccines is a huge lift. Then getting the vaccines to a clinical trial or outbreak setting quickly, safely, and efficiently is its own complex task.   Hear Noel Decker, MS, PMP, VP of Program & Portfolio Management on Sabin's R&D team, break down some of the challenges ⤵️

board.public_perception_text: Sabin's social media presence continues to strengthen institutional reputation. Our messaging reaches diverse stakeholder groups with strong engagement metrics. Positive sentiment reflects public confidence in our vaccine research and immunization initiatives.
board.donor_engagement_text: Social channels serve as critical touchpoints for demonstrating research impact and organizational effectiveness. Quarterly reports of breakthrough achievements drive stakeholder engagement and support fundraising objectives. Expanding reach indicates growing influence in vaccine policy discussions.
board.risk_management_text: Consistent engagement monitoring identifies potential reputational risks early. Current positioning addresses vaccine concerns and establishes Sabin as trusted authority. Social media serves as early warning system enabling rapid response to misinformation.

assumptions: Reach and impressions are standardized into one visibility metric per platform, using impressions when available and otherwise reach.
Report-facing summary cards use Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn only so the dashboard and quarterly report share one scope.
Cross-network post engagements continue to come from Hootsuite's Post engagement aggregate, with X removed when legacy X totals are present.
Detailed platform, program, and post layers continue to use standardized post-level exports where available, and link clicks stay separate from engagement totals.
Owly link-click exports are treated as website-resource traffic enrichment for Facebook and LinkedIn posts; X/Twitter Owly tables are optional when present.
YouTube follower counts remain available in raw Hootsuite exports, but report-facing summary cards exclude YouTube until a matching platform detail layer is maintained.
Actual follower pace uses real January 1 follower counts when they can be recovered from January exports or saved January dashboard artifacts.
Target pace remains a separate benchmark derived from the stated year-end target and annual growth rate.
Monthly export completeness is complete only when the cross-platform aggregate export, all full post-performance exports, and the expected Facebook/LinkedIn Owly website-click exports are present.
Email exports are excluded from social platform calculations to avoid mixing unlike metrics.
Follower pace is labeled slightly behind when actual performance is within 5% of the benchmark pace.

The cross-platform aggregate account_metrics export is the all-platform rollup, and supplemental top-post files may still be needed to support post-level context where full post-performance exports are missing.
